title: India Refuse Asia Cup Trophy From Naqvi Again After Women's Team Wins Final
excerpt: Harmanpreet Kaur's side beat Sri Lanka by 72 runs in Dubai to win an eighth Women's Asia Cup, then stayed away from the presentation stage as ACC president Mohsin Naqvi waited — repeating the men's team's 2025 stand.
body:
• India's women declined to collect the Women's Asia Cup trophy from ACC president Mohsin Naqvi after a 72-run final win over Sri Lanka in Dubai.
  • The ceremony was delayed about 40 minutes; Naqvi handed Sri Lanka the runners-up cheque while the champions stayed away from the stage.
  • Head coach Amol Muzumdar said the decision was taken by the BCCI: "We stand by it. We are the champions. That's good enough."
  • It mirrors the men's 2025 final, when Suryakumar Yadav's India also declined Naqvi's trophy amid strained India-Pakistan ties.

India lifted the Women's Asia Cup on Sunday night in Dubai and left the presentation stage empty. Minutes after a 72-run win over Sri Lanka, the champions refused to collect the trophy from Asian Cricket Council president Mohsin Naqvi — replaying the men's team's stand against the same man a year ago.

Chasing 183 for five, Sri Lanka were bowled out for 111. Shafali Verma's 68 off 39 balls and Smriti Mandhana's 59 off 39 powered the total; Sree Charani's four-wicket haul and Deepti Sharma's three wickets finished the job — India's eighth Women's Asia Cup title in ten editions, and its fourth in the T20I format.

The ceremony was delayed by roughly 40 minutes. Sri Lanka's players took the stage for their runners-up medals, with captain Chamari Athapaththu accepting a cheque from Naqvi — ACC president, PCB chairman, and Pakistan's interior minister. After Sri Lanka's presentation concluded, the broadcast cut back to the studio. India's players never appeared.

Stadium footage showed sections of the crowd chanting "trophy chor" (trophy thief) as Naqvi appeared on the podium. India later held its own medal ceremony with BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia and board vice-president Rajiv Shukla.

"We stand by it. For us, this tournament is over. We are the champions. That's good enough. We are united. I am proud of every single person in this unit, including the sports staff and the players."

— Amol Muzumdar, India head coach

Context & Background

The message was sent before the final. India refused to shake hands with Pakistan's players before and after matches through the tournament, including the women's seven-wicket group-stage win over Pakistan earlier this month. Coach Amol Muzumdar told reporters the trophy decision was taken by the BCCI, and the team stands behind it.

The precedent is a year old. In September 2025, India's men beat Pakistan in the Dubai final and refused the winners' trophy from Naqvi. That ceremony was delayed by more than an hour as the Indian players stayed put about 15 yards away; team management had asked who would present the trophy, and the ACC knew its chairman was unacceptable to the champions.

Fans booed Naqvi with chants of "Bharat Maata Ki Jai" as he took the dais. Told the champions would not accept the trophy from him, he waited on while an official took the trophy into the dressing room; Pakistan's players did not emerge for nearly an hour.

"I think this is one thing which I have never seen since I started playing cricket, started following cricket, that a champion team is denied a trophy, that too a hard-earned one. I feel we deserved it... If you tell me about trophies, my trophies are sitting in the dressing room, all the 14 guys with me, the support staff, those are the real trophies throughout this journey in the Asia Cup."

— Suryakumar Yadav, India men's captain, September 2025

The backdrop is political: a brief May 2025 military conflict that nearly became full-scale war. The countries play no bilateral cricket, meeting only in ICC and ACC events on neutral venues. The trophy snubs, handshake boycotts, and skipped pre-toss photoshoots are all of a piece with that freeze.

Impact & Analysis

Two Asia Cup finals in two years have ended with the champions refusing the trophy from the tournament's own president — corrosive optics for the ACC, whose marquee event now concludes with an empty podium.

India's stance has moved from one-off gesture to standing policy, announced by the board and executed by two different teams. The ACC must now decide whether to keep Naqvi at the presentation dais knowing India will not come forward, or quietly restructure its ceremonies. Reuters has requested comment from the ACC.

Diaspora Angle

Dubai's stadiums fill with Indian fans, and Sunday's "trophy chor" chants came from that crowd. Across the diaspora in the US, UK, and Canada, opinion split between celebrating the refusal as principle and arguing sport should stay separate from politics.

What's Next

The two sides could meet again at the Asian Games in Japan later this month — and produce another presentation ceremony. The BCCI has shown no sign of softening, and the ACC has yet to explain its presentation protocol for next time.
image_caption: ACC president Mohsin Naqvi at the stadium during the Women's Asia Cup 2026 final in Dubai. India's players stayed away from the presentation stage as he waited to hand over the trophy.
